args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 began failing health checks after deployment to production (error rate 18%, unhealthy in us-east, us-west, eu-west). v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. The service was rolled back in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 regression and why it was promoted despite unhealthy staging RC.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident, which paged on-call.

- **What went wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, was failing health checks and had an 18% error rate. Its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had also been unhealthy in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. It's now running in all three regions. A follow-up check shows the service healthy, with the error rate down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open. It describes the v2.3.1 failure and the rollback to v2.3.0. It also suggests looking into the v2.3.1 bug and why that version reached production when its release candidate had failed in staging. I opened it at the same time as the health check, so it doesn't mention that the service has recovered. You may want to add that.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
